question: Which of the following is an isobar of argon?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Isobars are atoms of different chemical elements that have the same number of nucleons (protons + neutrons).
 
• Argon has an atomic number of 18 and a common isotope with a mass number of 40 (Argon-40).
 
• Calcium has an atomic number of 20 and a common isotope with a mass number of 40 (Calcium-40).
 
• Since both Argon-40 and Calcium-40 have the same mass number, they are isobars.
 
• Isobars of different elements differ in chemical properties but have similar atomic masses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isotopes vs. Isobars:**

 
 
• Isotopes are atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons and different mass numbers.
 
• Isobars are atoms of different elements with the same mass number but different atomic numbers.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Isobars:**
 
 
• Isobars are used in various scientific fields, including nuclear physics and chemistry, to study nuclear reactions and stability.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Isobars:**
 
 
• Argon-40 and Calcium-40 are examples of isobars.
 
• Other examples include Carbon-14 and Nitrogen-14.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Isobars:**
 
 
• Isobars are used in medical applications, such as in radiopharmaceuticals for imaging and treatment.
 
• They are also used in geological dating and tracing environmental changes.
